parsed.notes: Lens B only; support and quote fidelity were not audited.

reasons: The lake identity record is verified and matches Mullenix v. Luna, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2015-11-09.
The disclosed citations include 577 U.S. 7, 136 S. Ct. 305, 193 L. Ed. 2d 255, and 2015 U.S. LEXIS 7160.
The lake treatment field marks the authority good_law as of 2026-06-30, so Lens B has no disclosed basis to say the authority is not live law.
residual_risks: The lake warns that official cite selection failed closed, but that is a citation-classification risk, not a disclosed currency defect.

reasons: Support classification is not Lens B's charter, but the disclosed currency record does not undermine the home-role assertion.
The lake progeny record reports 756 indexed citing opinions and citation_count 3491, consistent with a significant progeny/refinement role.
The top-level treatment remains good_law with no point_overrides.
residual_risks: Lens B did not audit editorial fit or support depth for the home-role label.

reasons: Support and quote fidelity are not Lens B's charter, but the treatment scope note directly preserves the asserted point: good law on the specificity of clearly established law for qualified immunity.
No disclosed point_override limits that proposition.
The authority is marked good_law as of 2026-06-30.
residual_risks: Lens B did not test quote fidelity or full holding support.

reasons: The lake identity record sets court_level to scotus and court to U.S. Supreme Court.
A U.S. Supreme Court merits authority marked good_law supports the page weight label Binding - SCOTUS.
No disclosed treatment field or point_override strips the case of binding Supreme Court weight.
residual_risks: The proposed treatment edges create audit risk for treatment wording, but not for the SCOTUS weight label itself.

defect.locator_note: treatment field and Treatment & subsequent history section
defect.problem: The core good_law call survives, but the page's unqualified treatment prose is too strong. The lake has audit-needed proposed progeny/treatment edges with negative labels, so the disclosed record supports 'no confirmed negative treatment' rather than an unconditional no-negative-treatment statement.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep field_i_validity as good_law on the specificity point, but change treatment prose to say there is no confirmed negative treatment in the disclosed lake record and that proposed treatment edges remain unaudited.

reasons: The lake top-level treatment says field_i_validity good_law, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, and scope_note good law on the specificity of clearly established law for qualified immunity.
The same treatment record contains 26 proposed edges with field_ii labels including overruled, questioned, abrogated, and criticized, all marked proposed and field_iii mentioned.
Because those edges are proposed rather than confirmed, they do not by themselves refute good_law, but they do require a caveat before saying there is no negative treatment.
residual_risks: If any proposed edge is later confirmed as actual negative treatment of Mullenix or a specific point in Mullenix, field_i_validity or point_overrides may need revision.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use: Good law on the specificity of clearly established law for qualified immunity as of 2026-06-30; no confirmed point override in the disclosed lake record, with proposed treatment edges still requiring audit.
